h1: Phunaya Resort Khao Kho — a budget hillside stay with both cabins and a campsite
intro: Not everyone who comes to Khao Kho wants to pay for a luxury resort costing several thousand a night. Some just want a clean room on the hillside, cool air, and a mountain view when you open the door, at a price you don't have to think twice about — Phunaya Resort, or Phunaya Resort Khao Kho, is that kind of place · It's a small cabin resort in Khao Kho district, Phetchabun province, just about 9.5 km from town, with air-con cabins, cottages, family rooms, and a hillside campsite under the name Rai Phunaya · Rates start from a few hundred to the low thousands · Based on real guest reviews, it scores around 7.7–8.0 among Khao Kho's budget stays.

body.html: Overview and who it suits — To put it in the shortest way, Phunaya Resort Khao Kho is a small budget hillside stay that positions itself for people who want to visit Khao Kho without spending a lot on the room · It's not a fully themed resort with flower gardens and a castle for photos, and it's not a luxury boutique that sells design at every angle · Instead it's a simple cabin resort with a straightforward selling point: an affordable price, a location close to Phetchabun town, and both rooms and a campsite in one place · The registered address is 70 Moo 5, Khao Kho subdistrict, Khao Kho district, just about 9.5 km from town · Pulling together real reviews on Tripadvisor, Traveloka, Agoda, and Khao Kho review pages, the picture is fairly consistent that the people it suits best are budget travelers, couples who want a quiet bed on the hillside, groups of friends into camping, and families who value good value over luxury · Another group that finds it worthwhile is people using Khao Kho as a stopover or a single overnight before traveling on, because it's close to town and the main road, with no deep mountain drive like many of the popular resorts · As for anyone expecting the full range of amenities of a big hotel, with a pool, spa, or five-star service, set your expectations first, because this is a small resort that sells simplicity and price above all, not a complete set of services.

Location and getting there — Where Phunaya has the edge over many Khao Kho resorts is that it's close to Phetchabun town, just about 9.5 km away, or roughly a 15–20 min drive · That means if you arrive late, get hungry, or want to buy something, you can pop into town without trouble, with no long winding mountain drive like the resorts over by the pine camp or the wind turbine fields · Coming from Bangkok, most people drive themselves via the Saraburi–Lom Sak route, taking about 5–6 hr, or take a coach/van down to Phetchabun town and then a connecting ride to the resort · The nearest airport is Phitsanulok, which is a fair distance away and needs another ride of about 2 hr, so most people prefer to drive themselves · As for Khao Kho's main sights, it's only fair to say Phunaya is on the near-town side, not right by the highlights like Wat Phra That Pha Sorn Kaew or the wind turbine fields, which sit higher up the mountain · From the resort, driving to these main sights, you should allow around 30–50 min or more depending on the spot · The upside is that if you focus on quiet rest near town and then drive out sightseeing in batches, this location works well and saves on the fuel of climbing the mountain · One note from the reviews is that the final stretch into the resort is a side lane and partly dirt road, which can get muddy in the rainy season, so drive slowly and check the route on a map before you arrive, because a small stay's signage may not be as prominent as a big resort's.

"We stayed just one night before heading up to see the upper parts of Khao Kho. Very cheap compared to other places, the room was clean enough, and being close to town made it easy to drive in for food without a long mountain drive."

Rooms and decor — Phunaya is a small resort with around 10 units total, split into several styles to choose from by group size and budget · It starts with the Standard Air Conditioning room, the cheapest entry-level option, suited to couples or solo travelers who just want a clean, cool place to sleep · Stepping up is the Cottage, a small cabin offering more privacy, with a sitting terrace looking out over the garden and mountains · For families or groups of friends there's the Family Cottage and Family Bungalow, which sleep several people and suit coming as a group · Every room is air-conditioned, with drinking water and basic bathroom amenities, a TV, and a private terrace · The decor overall is a simple cabin-resort style, leaning on wood tones and easy-on-the-eyes comfort, not luxurious but looking clean and warm in an upcountry-cabin way · Most real reviews agree that the rooms are clean to a level that's solidly acceptable for the price, the beds sleep well, and the atmosphere is quiet · One note that comes up is that, being a small budget resort, some details follow the budget — for example, the bathrooms are shower-only with no bathtub, the furniture is the practical sort rather than design-focused, and some units may show signs of wear with age · Anyone coming in the cold season should check that the room they book has a water heater and enough thick blankets, because nighttime in the Khao Kho area really is cold.

Facilities and the campsite — You should understand first that Phunaya is a small resort, so the facilities are the basic essentials, with no pool, spa, or fitness center like a big resort · What it has and that actually works are free parking out front, Wi-Fi in the common area, an on-site restaurant, a garden and a sitting terrace with mountain views, and a barbecue grilling area · What sets Phunaya apart from typical budget stays is that it has a hillside campsite under the name Rai Phunaya Camping for people who want to sleep in a tent catching the mountain breeze and wake up to a mountain view, at a price lower than a room · This is an option that groups of friends into camping, and families who want their kids to experience the camping atmosphere, enjoy · Reviews of the campsite say the view and the air are good, a genuinely natural setting, but you do have to be ready for the camping reality, meaning the facilities are shared and simple · Overall, measured by price, Phunaya's facilities are fitting for a base to rest and stay overnight, rather than a resort where you spend the whole day inside like a full-service one · Anyone who wants plenty of on-site activities should plan instead to drive out to Khao Kho's various spots.

Food and the on-site restaurant — Phunaya has an on-site restaurant serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner, à la carte in Thai and local-style cooking · On breakfast, check carefully when you book, because some room rates don't include breakfast, so you need to book a package that includes it or pay extra yourself · Reviews of the food are fairly middle-of-the-road, in the style of a small resort, saying the food is decent enough, not pricey, and the setting of eating with a mountain view is nice, but the menu choices aren't very varied, and at quieter times you may have to order ahead or wait longer than usual · The upside of the location is that it's close to Phetchabun town, about 15–20 min, so you can easily drive in to find restaurants, cafés, and convenience stores in town, without relying on the resort restaurant alone · Many people therefore choose to eat their main meals out and use the resort as a place to sleep and rest · If you come as a group and want to grill your own food in the evening, the resort has a barbecue area, an activity that groups of friends and camping families like to do · We'd suggest asking the resort in advance about preparing the grill and ingredients, because it's a small stay and some extra services may need notice.

Service — Service at a small resort like Phunaya usually depends on the owner and the team looking after it directly, which is both a plus and a limitation · On the plus side, many reviews say the owner and staff are friendly and easy to talk to, and good at recommending places to go and eat around Khao Kho, giving the feeling of staying at a relative's place upcountry rather than a hotel · Booking and asking questions through the resort's Facebook page is also convenient and gets quick replies during working hours · The limitation to understand is that, being a small stay with a small team, some services aren't as fixed-standard as a chain hotel — for example, checking in outside normal hours, ordering food during quiet times, or asking for extra services may need advance notice and some flexibility · This is the nature of a small upcountry cabin resort rather than a quality problem · If you set expectations correctly that you're staying at a simple local place, most voices say you'll be looked after warmly and come away impressed by the friendliness.

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — Pulling together from Tripadvisor, Traveloka, Agoda, and Khao Kho stay-review pages, the picture is fairly consistent · It should be said first that Phunaya is a small stay whose number of reviews on the platforms isn't large yet, so the scores you see come from a small group of guests, but the direction of opinion is fairly aligned, with an overall score around 7.7–8.0 and Tripadvisor rating it "Good" · On the praise side: cheap and good value compared with other Khao Kho stays, a location close to town that's easy to reach without a long mountain drive, rooms clean enough for the price, cool comfortable air and a quiet atmosphere good for resting, a campsite as a budget option, and a friendly owner and staff · On the watch-out side: what gets mentioned is basic facilities, no pool or big-resort services, limited food choices at the resort, room and furniture details that follow the budget, a final entrance stretch that's a side lane/partly dirt road and can get muddy in the rainy season, and not being right by Khao Kho's main highlights, so you have to drive out · Most of these gripes are predictable from being a budget stay, and are manageable by setting expectations to match the price, rather than problems that leave people badly disappointed.

"It's not a luxury resort, but at this price it's really okay. The room was clean, the air cool, the owner lovely, and you can bring the kids to camp too. You just have to accept there's no pool and not a lot of things to do like a big resort."

Price and value compared — Phunaya's starting rates are among the cheapest in Khao Kho, with rooms and the campsite starting from a few hundred to the low thousands per night, depending on room type, time of year, and whether breakfast is included · Prices climb in the cold-season high season (November–January) and on long holidays, like Khao Kho stays in general, but overall they stay in a more accessible bracket than the area's themed or luxury boutique resorts that start from around two thousand and up · Compared with Khao Kho stays in a similar price range, Phunaya's value is that you get a hillside room, cool air, a location close to town, and a camping option all in one place, on a budget that doesn't squeeze the wallet · It suits people whose main goal is heading out to sightsee around Khao Kho all day and then coming back to sleep, rather than wanting to spend the whole day at the resort · Measured by the value a budget traveler or camper looks for, it's worthwhile · But if you want a pool, a peak sea-of-mist view from the terrace, or full-service amenities, you may need to add to the budget and pick an up-the-mountain resort that specifically sells the view and facilities instead.

Good to know before booking — A few things help make the stay smoother · One, check clearly whether the room you book includes breakfast, because some types don't and you'll need to pay extra; if you want breakfast, pick a package that includes it at the time of booking · Two, if you plan to camp, ask the resort ahead about equipment — whether tents are available to rent or you need to bring your own — as well as bathrooms and electricity at the campsite · Three, pack warm clothes and bring an extra blanket if you come in the cold season, because you're in the Khao Kho area and the nights really are cold, especially if you sleep in a tent · Four, because it's a small stay and the sign may not be prominent, open a navigation map and call the resort to ask the route before you arrive, especially if you get there in the evening · Five, book and ask for the latest details directly through Agoda or the resort's Facebook page, because at a small stay prices and availability change with the season · Six, plan the upper Khao Kho sights in batches in advance, because the resort is on the near-town side and driving up to the various highlights means allowing travel time.

The verdict — From all the real reviews, Phunaya Resort Khao Kho is the stay that suits best for budget travelers, couples, groups of friends into camping, and families who value good value over luxury · Its strengths are an easy-to-reach price, a location close to Phetchabun town with no long mountain drive, both rooms and a campsite in one place, and the friendliness of a local stay, making it a worthwhile base to rest and stay overnight before or after heading out to Khao Kho's various spots · But if you're looking for a resort with a pool, a sea-of-mist view from the terrace, full-service amenities, or on-site activities to fill the whole day, this may not be the answer, and you should add to the budget and pick an up-the-mountain resort that specifically sells the view and facilities · But for a Khao Kho trip where you want to save on the room so you can spend on sightseeing and food, or want to try sleeping in a tent catching the mountain air at an easy-on-the-wallet price — Phunaya meets that need squarely, and it's an option that Khao Kho's budget travelers have always talked about for its value.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Phunaya Resort Khao Kho

faq.q: Where is Phunaya Resort Khao Kho · is it easy to reach?
faq.a: It's at 70 Moo 5, Khao Kho subdistrict, Khao Kho district, Phetchabun province, on the near-town side · Just about 9.5 km from Phetchabun town, or a 15–20 min drive, with no long winding mountain drive, so it's easy to pop into town for food and supplies · Khao Kho's main upper sights, like the royal palace, the wind turbine fields, and Wat Pha Sorn Kaew, mean a drive out of around 30–50 min.

faq.q: What are Phunaya Resort's starting rates · what room types are there?
faq.a: Starting rates are among the cheapest in Khao Kho, a few hundred to the low thousands per night · There are around 10 units in several styles, including standard air-con rooms, cottages, family rooms, and family bungalows, plus a campsite (Rai Phunaya) as a budget option · Cold-season and holiday prices climb, and some room types don't include breakfast, so check clearly before booking.

faq.q: Who does Phunaya Resort suit best?
faq.a: It's a great fit for budget travelers, couples, groups of friends into camping, and families who value good value, who want a hillside bed with cool air at an easy-on-the-wallet price · It suits being a base to rest and stay overnight before or after heading out to Khao Kho's various spots, more than people who want a pool or big-resort service.

faq.q: Does Phunaya Resort really have a campsite · what's it like?
faq.a: Yes · The resort runs a hillside campsite under the name Rai Phunaya Camping for people who want to sleep in a tent catching the mountain breeze and wake up to a mountain view, at a price lower than a room · It's a simple natural setting with shared facilities · We'd suggest asking ahead whether tents are available to rent or you need to bring your own, and pack warm clothes.

faq.q: Does Phunaya Resort have a pool and food?
faq.a: No pool, because it's a small budget resort · It has an on-site restaurant serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner and a BBQ grilling area · On breakfast, check whether the room you book includes it · The upside is that it's close to town, about 15–20 min, so you can easily drive in to find restaurants and cafés in town.

faq.q: Where can you book Phunaya Resort?
faq.a: You can book through Agoda and travel platforms like Traveloka, Tripadvisor, and Hotels.com · You can also ask about availability, the latest rates, and camping directly through the Phunaya Resort Khao Kho Facebook page, which replies quickly during working hours · Because it's a small stay, prices and availability change with the season, so compare a few channels before booking.
